Meet Our Curators

Meet the minds behind your next favorite read. The SoulBox curation team is brought to life on our site through unique illustrated portraits, keeping our focus exactly where it belongs: on your bookshelf. Our real human experts collaborate daily to match exceptional literature to your soul. You get the focused expertise of a true boutique book team, wrapped in a classic literary style.

Rija

Rija reads like it's urgent. Not because she's racing through books — she's not — but because she genuinely believes the right story at the right moment changes something in you that can't be unchanged.

She's not interested in books that are merely good. She wants the ones that know things. The ones that understand how it feels to be a person — specifically, how hard it is, and how worth it.

If something's sitting heavy with you right now, she'll find it in your quiz. She always does.

“Fiction is the only place where other people's pain makes complete sense.”

Taniyah

Taniyah has strong opinions and she's not apologising for them. She thinks most people play it too safe with books — reaching for comfort when what they actually need is to be cracked open a little.

She'll pick you something that asks something of you. Not difficult for the sake of it. Just — honest. Real. The kind of book you put down and then pick back up three minutes later because you weren't done with it yet.

She's looking for the readers who are ready for that. Maybe that's you.

“I feel some books you finish and some books finish you. I'm looking for the second kind.”

Sienna

Sienna is quieter than the others about what she loves, which is probably why she's so good at finding it.

She reads slowly. She annotates. She has opinions about endings that she'll share only if you ask, and then she won't stop. She thinks a book that asks nothing of you is essentially just wallpaper — pretty, forgettable, not worth your time.

She suits readers who want to be taken seriously. Who don't just want a good read — they want the right one.

“A book that asks nothing of you is a book that gives you nothing back.”

Claire

Claire will fight you about your favourite book and she means it affectionately.

She's the one who has a genuine theory about why certain people are drawn to certain genres, and the theory is usually right, and it's usually a little uncomfortably specific. She reads your quiz answers like they're telling her something you didn't quite mean to say.

She's warm. She's sharp. She won't send you something safe unless safe is genuinely what you need.

“I've never trusted someone who says they don't have a favourite.”

Lucas

Lucas thinks timing is everything. The same book at 22 and 34 are two completely different books — he'll tell you this unprompted and he's not wrong.

He reads across everything. Literary fiction, genre, translated stuff, things that are hard to categorise. He's less interested in what you like and more interested in where you are right now — what you're ready for, what you're not, what you need to sit with before you're ready to move.

He's patient. His picks tend to stay with people.

“The right book at the wrong time is still the wrong book.”

Ahmed

Ahmed is the one who still gets genuinely excited. Not performatively — actually excited. He'll finish something at 1am and want to tell someone immediately and there's no one to tell.

He believes books are magic and he doesn't care if that sounds ridiculous. He's not interested in cynicism about reading, about fiction, about any of it. Life's too short and there are too many extraordinary books.

His readers tend to come back. That probably says something.

“Stories are genuinely magic.”
